description.narrative: The project is relevant to local entrepreneurs, female farmers, and youth because it will strengthen the capacity of young students, enabling them to become representatives to disseminate findings from surveys on various challenges that local entrepreneurs are facing, at provincial and national level meetings/forums. Furthermore, this proposed project directly relates to farmers and entrepreneurs, local conditions, challenges, and the issues mentioned above. The project will focus on fostering collaboration between entrepreneurs and youth in implementing CSA through participatory research studies, as well as providing technical support, including training on environmentally friendly agricultural techniques, and enabling youth to experiment with new innovations. The voices of youthin this project will help farmers adopt smarter production methods to access markets and connect with entrepreneur groups seeking to support CSA more sustainably. It will also help reduce negative environmental impacts, improve soil quality, reduce the use of harmful chemicals, and generate additional income for communities. Entrepreneur groups in Luang Prabang also face challenges in sourcing CSA products from farmers. The project aims for young students to become voices contributing to the promotion of sustainable growth in the agriculture and environmental sectors, enabling adaptation to climate change. This will be achieved by advocating for policy improvements concerning local producers and promoting behavioral change among farmers towards environmentally friendly production methods. The project's objective is to build the capacity of youth to research various challenges that entrepreneurs are facing, andto raise awareness among youth and farmers, particularly women and youth, about new agricultural models through experimenting with new innovations to reduce the use of chemicals harmful to health and the environment. Project Outcomes After the project concludes, 10 university students (including 5 women) will be ableto serve as voices for 30 vegetable and fruit farming entrepreneurs, using their research findings to advocate for policy changes. Additionally, 30 students from Souphanouvong University (15 women) and 16 farmers (8 women) from 4 target villages in XiengNgeun and Chomphet districts will understand the impacts of slash-and-burn agriculture and chemical use on climate change. They will be inspired to change their own behaviors and those of their communities regarding production and support for environmentally friendly agricultural products.

participating-org.narrative:
Our organization has a vision to create, establish, and build compassionate communities where people live in dignity through a continuous and participatory process for sustainable development. Namjai Community Association will work to promote sustainableand transformational development in communities and society, and advocacy to change the root causes of poverty and injustice. We will work with and for ethnic communities in cooperation with relevant authorities and development partners. We are guided by05 core values: 1.Human Dignity. Human dignity encompasses all humanity from the beginning to the end of life, irrespective of class, gender, faith or ethnicity. 2. Equality. All humans have the right to life, health, shelter, education, work, the freepractice of faith and equality before the law 3. Inclusive Communities. As human we are dependent on each other, with rights and responsibilities for our common life 4. Compassion. As human being we need to transform indifference, share love with everyone and act accordingly. 5. Accountability. We strive for open and honest communication, transparent practices in all our activities, finance and resources management
Our understanding of human dignity builds on the belief that all human beings havefundamental value and unique talents to share, irrespective of faith, culture, gender, sexual orientation, age, functional abilities or ethnicity. Human dignity is the foundation of the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights, which represents the world's longing for well-being, justice and security for all peoples and all nations. This inspires us to work on an agenda of gender and rights of the ethnic minorities.
